original_value: The detection of water pipeline leakage is important to ensure that water supply networks can operate safely and conserve water resources. To address the lack of intelligent and the low efficiency of conventional leakage detection methods, this paper designs a leakage detection method based on machine learning and wireless sensor networks (WSNs). The system employs wireless sensors installed on pipelines to collect data and utilizes the 4G network to perform remote data transmission. A leakage triggered networking method is proposed to reduce the wireless sensor network’s energy consumption and prolong the system life cycle effectively. To enhance the precision and intelligence of leakage detection, we propose a leakage identification method that employs the intrinsic mode function, approximate entropy, and principal component analysis to construct a signal feature set and that uses a support vector machine (SVM) as a classifier to perform leakage detection. Simulation analysis and experimental results indicate that the proposed leakage identification method can effectively identify the water pipeline leakage and has lower energy consumption than the networking methods used in conventional wireless sensor networks.

result.paraphrase: Detecting water pipeline leaks is essential for the safe operation of water supply networks and for conserving water resources. To overcome the poor intelligence and low efficiency of conventional leakage detection methods, this paper proposes a machine-learning-based leakage detection approach combined with wireless sensor networks (WSNs). Wireless sensors mounted on pipelines collect data, which are transmitted remotely via the 4G network. A leakage-triggered networking scheme is introduced to reduce wireless sensor network energy consumption and effectively extend system lifetime. To improve leakage detection accuracy and intelligence, a leakage identification method is proposed that uses intrinsic mode function, approximate entropy, and principal component analysis to build a signal feature set, with a support vector machine (SVM) classifier for leak detection. Simulation analysis and experimental results show that the proposed method can effectively identify water pipeline leakage while consuming less energy than conventional wireless sensor network networking methods.
